sec.title: Perforator substudy
sec.p: For the perforator substudy, we will perform a Doppler ultrasound of the patient before they undergo surgery. This Doppler ultrasound will be performed by a trained surgical oncologist who will map the perforators at the intercostal spaces below the inframammary crease and along the anterior axillary lines. Presence of a sound signal in the Doppler ultrasound would be considered as proof of vascular patency. Doppler sound recording would be saved for future reference and analysis.

sec.title: Justification for endpoint (DFS)
sec.p: The primary outcome measure for the trial is to demonstrate that neoadjuvant radiotherapy results in an improved invasive disease-free survival as compared to adjuvant radiotherapy. Therefore, a superiority trial has been designed. DFS is an appropriate surrogate endpoint given its strong positive correlation with overall survival [34]. All cancer-related endpoints in the study have been adopted from the Definition for the Assessment of Time-to-event Endpoints in CANcer trials (DATECAN) initiative and they have been aligned with the definitions proposed by DATECAN [33].

sec.title: Justification of targeted difference in DFS
sec.p: Three year DFS outcomes have been analysed from the patients enrolled in the HYPORT Adjuvant trial as a part of the 2nd interim analysis. Among 401 patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy, 51 patients had an event of interest and the 3-year estimate of the DFS was 78% (95% CI 73–84%).

We expect that the study will accrue participants over 60 months and a further follow-up 24 months will be needed making the total study duration of 7 years. We further assume that use of NART will result in an improved DFS at 3 years from 85% in the control arm to 89.8% in the neoadjuvant radiotherapy arm (absolute improvement of ~ 5%, hazard ratio of 0.65).

As per the ESMO MCBS Grade A (substantial magnitude of clinical benefit) is indicated when improvement of DFS of < 0.65 is obtained in studies without mature survival data. In studies with mature survival data, a 5% improvement in survival at 3 years or more follow-up is recommended. Hence, this threshold has been chosen for this trial.

sec.title: Sample size for primary outcome
sec.p: We further assume a 5% annual dropout from the trial. Two interim analyses have been planned for the study. Sample size has been calculated with a type I error rate of 2.5% and power of 80%. The total calculated sample size is 1121 patients distributed equally among the four arms. The number of patients that need to be accrued per month is 19. This matches well with the accrual rate observed in HYPORT Adjuvant where 12 patients receiving NACT have been accrued monthly on average.

The two interim analyses are planned, the first at 43 months and the second at 63.3 months. The first interim analysis will be planned when 54 events have been observed and at this stage the critical p value for futility is 0.688 and p value efficacy is < 0.001. The second interim analysis will be planned when 90 events have been observed and at this stage the critical p value for futility is 0.302 and p value efficacy is 0.0015. Sample size calculation was performed using the rpact package (version 3.3.4) [39]. For time to event endpoints, the package allows sample size calculation using Schoenfeld’s formula [40]. An O’Brien & Fleming type alpha spending and an O’Brien & Fleming type beta spending function are used with a non-binding futility for the interim analyses.
The following table shows the details of the sample size computation.

Sample sizes have been computed for 3 year DFS of 80% and 75% which are plausible estimates from the HYPORT adjuvant for the patients receiving adjuvant radiotherapy. The same assumptions are made and an improvement has been targeted with a hazard ratio of 0.65. Sample sizes were 849 and 685 patients.

sec.title: Sample size for breast/chest wall induration
sec.p: In the study two schedules of radiation dose fractionation are also being evaluated. Given the results of the FAST Forward trial as well as the interim analysis of the HYPORT Adjuvant trial (presented to DSMC), we do not expect a significant difference between the two dose schedules for cancer outcomes. However, late normal tissue effects are of interest and would need evaluation. We have chosen induration of the breast and chest wall induration as this is an event noted with a greater frequency receiving a five fraction regimen of radiotherapy in the FAST Forward trial and can be assessed in patients who have undergone breast conservation and mastectomy [16]. In the FAST Forward trial, moderate to severe clinician-reported breast induration in the tumour bed was documented in 25 of 914 patients in the control arm (4%). In the patient receiving a dose of 26 Gy in 5 fractions, the same was seen in 39 of 956 patients (5%, RR 1.49). Moderate to severe breast induration outside the tumour bed was documented in 1 patient in the control arm versus 20 patients in the patients receiving 26 Gy in 5 fractions (RR 19.2). Patient-reported outcomes of breast feeling harder or firmer corroborated this finding (odds ratio 1.22, 95% CI 1.00–1.48).

For this study extrapolating from the data in the FAST Forward trial, we will assume that the probabilities of patient reported no, mild, moderate and severe induration in the breast or chest wall in the patients receiving a 3-week regimen are 55%, 30%, 9% and 6% respectively. Using a two-tailed two sample comparison of ordinal outcomes under the proportional odds ordinal logistic model, the sample size of 1121 patients will provide us with a power of 0.83 to detect an odds ratio of ≥ 1.4 with a type I error of 5%. This sample size has been calculated using the power function available in the Hmisc package (version 4.7.1) [41].

sec.title: Sample size for substudy I: perforator substudy
sec.p: Currently, the perforator detection rate is 100%. As per the discussion with the surgical oncologists, a detection rate of 90% or lower would be considered unacceptable. In this case we do not expect that patients receiving NART will have a better perforator detection rate. Given these parameters, a sample size of 19 patients will provide a power of 80% and a one sided type I error rate of 5% to detect a non-identification of 10% or more in the experimental arms (assuming a non-identification rate of 0.01% in the patients receiving ART). Hence a total 40 patients (20 in each arm) undergoing NART will be needed for this substudy.

sec.title: Sample size for substudy II: sentinel identification
sec.p: Sentinel lymph node non-identification rate in patients undergoing sentinel lymph node biopsy is 99% (i.e., in 1% patients sentinel lymph nodes are not detectable after NACT). It would be acceptable to have a non-identification rate up to 10%. A sample of 114 patients (52 patients in each arm) would allow us to detect this difference between NART vs ART with a one sided type I error of 10% and a power of 80% (sample size calculation method by Fliess et al., 1980—via calculator implemented on https://stattools.crab.org).

sec.title: Sample size for pathological complete response rate substudy
sec.p: It is expected that use of neoadjuvant radiotherapy will translate into an improved pathological complete response rate. Based on the results of patients enrolled in the HYPORT adjuvant trial, we know that pathological complete response rate after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (defined a ypT0 N0 status) is 26% (152 of 586 patients). The response rate is higher in patients with HER2 enriched tumours (68/206, 33%) and triple negative breast cancers (55/159, 35%) as compared to luminal cancers (29/217, 13%). Assuming that the pathological complete response in patients receiving neoadjuvant radiotherapy is 30% (we can expect some improvements due to increased use of platinum in triple negative breast cancer patients), a sample size of 256 patients provides us with a one sided type I error of 5% and power of 80% to detect an absolute improvement of 15% in the pathological complete response rate (i.e. 45%) with the use of neoadjuvant radiotherapy.

Note that patients enrolled in the wound complication substudy will be eligible for the pathological complete response rate substudy also. No additional assessments are required for the substudy. Approximately 14 months will be required to complete accrual into this substudy.

sec.title: Sample size for wound complication rate substudy
sec.p: Assuming that the Grade III-V wound complication rate in the control arm is 5% or less, an absolute increase of up to 10–20% can be considered acceptable in this scenario if this is associated with an improved disease-free survival. This would place our results in line with previous reports of neoadjuvant radiotherapy which report a wound complication rate ranging between 12 and 39% after NACT. Further as the patient has already received radiotherapy prior to surgery, a higher rate of wound complication will not delay further therapy.

A total sample of 498 patients (249 receiving NART and 249 receiving ART) will allow us to detect a 5% absolute increase in grade III–IV wound complication in patients receiving neoadjuvant radiotherapy as compared to patients receiving upfront surgery where we assume that wound complication rate would be 5% with a one sided type I error of 10% and a power of 80%.

In addition to comparison of wound complication rate between the trial and control arms, we will also compare the wound complication rate between the two trial arms. In the above scenario, we would be able to exclude a 10% increase in the wound complication rate between the Test Arm-1 and Test Arm-2 with a power of 82% and a one sided type I error of 150%, assuming that the wound complication rate is 10% in Test Arm-1.
Based on the planned accrual rate of 19 patients per month, 26 months will be required to accrue the patients for this substudy.

sec.title: Recruitment {15}
sec.p: Each participating centre would screen subjects and determine eligibility for inclusion in the trial. The recruitment period is expected to last for 60 months. Patients will be recruited from the outpatient departments of the participating centres. No financial reimbursement shall be provided to the participants in the trial. Patients can be screened at any point of time before or during the initiation of neoadjuvant chemotherapy for the trial. But randomisation will be done only after the neoadjuvant chemotherapy is completed. The rationale for post neoadjuvant chemotherapy randomisation is that this will allow us to ensure that the supraclavicular and internal mammary nodal status is assessed before the start of the neoadjuvant radiotherapy.

sec.title: Sequence generation {16a}
sec.p: Participants will be randomly assigned to either the control or one of the three experimental groups as per a computer-generated randomisation schedule. Stratification variables will include the following:

list-item.p: Oestrogen receptor status: Positive vs Negative
Progesterone receptor status: Positive vs Negative
HER2 neu receptor status: Positive vs Negative vs Equivocal

sec.p: Randomisation sequence will be generated using a computer programme using permuted blocks of random sizes.

sec.title: Concealment mechanism {16b}
sec.p: The block sizes will not be disclosed to ensure concealment. Randomisation table will be uploaded on the REDCap database for the study and this will be used for computerised central randomisation of the participants in the trial. Allocation concealment will be ensured, as the form will not allow randomisation until the patient has been recruited into the trial, provided informed consent and all baseline details to determine eligibility have been entered in the system.

sec.title: Implementation {16c}
sec.p: Patients will be randomised using REDCap hosted at Tata Medical Center. Randomisation is performed by the trial coordinators using the electronic system. The allocation sequence will be generated by the designated trial statistician and uploaded to the REDCap randomisation module before the project is initiated.

sec.title: Who will be blinded {17a}
sec.p: Given the nature of the interventions planned in the trial, no blinding is planned.

sec.title: Procedure for unblinding if needed {17b}
sec.p: As this is an open-label trial, unblinding is not required.

sec.title: Plans for assessment and collection of outcomes {18a}
sec.p: Data will be collected using case record forms designed and hosted on an electronic research data capture tool—REDCap hosted at Tata Medical Center, Kolkata. All participating institutes will also have access to the same REDCap database. REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture) is a secure, web-based software platform designed to support data capture for research studies, providing (1) an intuitive interface for validated data capture; (2) audit trails for tracking data manipulation and export procedures; (3) automated export procedures for seamless data downloads to common statistical packages; and (4) procedures for data integration and interoperability with external sources [42, 43]. In the clinic, electronic data may be captured directly on the electronic CRFs or may be transcribed from paper CRFs completed in the clinic. In case the latter is done, paper records should be saved in a study-specific participant file. If patient-reported outcomes are collected electronically in a system separate from REDCap, a mechanism must be in place which allows import of the patient-reported data in the REDCap database.

sec.title: Plans to promote participant retention and complete follow-up {18b}
sec.p: Patients will be treated at the primary treating centre and will continue follow-up under the clinical team. For patients unable to attend outpatient clinics, telemedicine follow-ups are allowed.

sec.title: Data management {19}
sec.p: Access to the data will be available to the principal investigator of the study as well as to the co-investigators. The data quality and integrity will be checked at quarterly intervals using the data quality checking system available in Redcap. Patient identifiers will be noted as such in the Redcap database and the same will be used for ensuring that any data exports contain de-identified data only. Institutes will have access to the data of their own institute during the trial phase. Once the trial is completed, the main database will be checked for data consistency and quality and then closed for analysis. Additionally, the PI will be asked to sign off key CRFs electronically to ensure completeness and accuracy of the data.

Source documents pertaining to the trial must be maintained by investigational sites. Source documents may include a subject’s medical records, hospital charts, clinic charts, the investigator’s subject study files, and the results of diagnostic tests such as X-rays, laboratory tests and electrocardiograms. The investigator’s copy of the case report forms serves as part of the investigator’s record of a subject’s study-related data. All study-related documentation will be maintained for 10 years following completion of the study or according to existing regulatory requirements.
The following information should be entered into the subject’s medical record:

list-item.p: Subject’s name, contact information and protocol identification.
The date that the subject entered the study, and the subject number.
A statement that informed consent was obtained (including the date).
Relevant medical history
Dates of all subject visits and results of key trial parameters.
Occurrence and status of any adverse events.
The date the subject exited the study, and a notation as to whether the subject completed the study or reason for discontinuation

sec.title: Confidentiality {27}
sec.p: The study will be conducted in accordance with applicable rules and regulations. All data generated in this study will remain confidential. All information will be stored securely at the Tata Medical Center and will only be available to staff directly involved with the study. For documents transferred between institutions the data will be securely stored in the REDCap database and access restricted to the trial institute and the CTU through the use the data access groups features in RedCap.

sec.title: Plans for collection, laboratory evaluation and storage of biological specimens for genetic or molecular analysis in this trial/future use {33}
sec.p: Imaging data of the patients including radiotherapy treatment plans will be de-identified and stored in the CHAVI image bank. If funding is available, a dedicated biobanking substudy will be set up.

sec.title: Statistical methods for primary and secondary analysis {20a}
sec.p: The complete details of the statistical analysis will be detailed in a statistical analysis plan. Cancer outcomes will be done using an intention to treat principle whilst for toxicity a per-protocol analysis will be conducted.

sec.title: Primary outcome
sec.p: For the primary endpoint (DFS) the outcomes of the patients receiving NART will be compared against the patients receiving ART. The primary endpoint of disease-free survival will be defined as the interval between the date of randomisation to date of appearance of the first event (locoregional recurrence, distant metastases, second malignancy including ductal carcinoma in situ of the breast) or death due to any cause. The comparison will be done using a Cox Proportional hazards model. The omnibus model will be adjusted for the dose fractionation schedule (3 week versus 1 week) and the stratification variables (oestrogen receptor status, progesterone receptor status and HER2 neu receptor status). An interaction term between the sequence of radiotherapy and dose fractionation used will be included in the omnibus model and the likelihood ratio test will be used to determine the significance of this interaction. Point estimates of the hazard ratio and the 95% confidence intervals will be reported. For every model, the underlying assumptions for the model will be checked which would include checks for proportional hazards assumptions, outlier and overly influential detection as well as a check for the linearity assumptions. Additionally bootstrapping will be used to estimate the calibration and discrimination of the model. P values < 0.05 will be considered statistically significant.

sec.title: Breast/chest wall induration
sec.p: Patient reported breast/chest wall induration will be compared between the 1-week and 3-week fractionation regimens. The trajectory of the primary endpoint over 36 months will be compared. A linear mixed model with an omnibus test where time is modelled as a discrete variable along with a time x dose-fractionation interaction will be used. The linear mixed model would be adjusted for the following covariates: baseline induration severity, age, radiotherapy sequence (NART vs ART), breast surgery type (Breast conservation vs Mastectomy), nodal staging type (axillary dissection versus sentinel lymph node biopsy) and regional nodal radiotherapy (delivered or not). Age will be modelled flexibly using restricted cubic splines with 4 knots. Graphical depiction of the patient-reported outcome scores over the assessment period will be provided. Missing data at each assessment time will be reported at the level of the instrument as well as at the level of the individual items. Based on the kind of dropout experienced for the patient-reported outcome an alternative joint model where the death or disease recurrence can stop the observation of the longitudinal outcome would also be considered. This will be used if the dropout in the QoL assessments is related to the disease recurrence or death in the trial [44]. Graphical summaries of the induration severity at each time point of measurement will also be provided.

sec.title: Additional cancer-related outcomes
sec.p: The analysis for other time to event endpoints will follow the same methodology as outlined for the primary outcome analysis. Separate models will be presented for each endpoint. Covariate adjustments and interaction testing will follow the same principles as outlined above.

sec.title: Patient-reported outcomes
sec.p: Patient-reported outcomes will be measured using the EORTC QLQ C30 and BR45 questionnaires in the trial. Both questionnaires provide scores for several functional and symptom scales. Standardised scores (ranging between 0 and 100) will be calculated for each of the functional and symptom scales from the questionnaire using the methodology proposed by the EORTC quality of life group. The EORTC QLQ C30 is a 30-item self-administered questionnaire that provides scores for five functional scales (physical functioning, role functioning, emotional functioning, cognitive functioning and social functioning), nine symptom scales (fatigue, nausea & vomiting, pain, diarrhoea, constipation, sleep disturbance, dyspnea, appetite loss and financial difficulties) and one global health and quality of life scale. The EORTC BR45 questionnaire provides scores for five functional scales (body image, future perspective, sexual functioning, sexual enjoyment and breast satisfaction) along with four symptom scales (systemic therapy side effects, upset by hair loss and arm symptoms).

As with the patient reported breast/chest wall induration, a linear mixed model or a joint model will be used for comparing the patient-reported outcomes (scores for each of the scales) between the radiotherapy sequence (NART vs ART). A linear mixed model with an omnibus test where time is modelled as a discrete variable along with a time x radiotherapy-sequence interaction will be used. The models will be adjusted for baseline scale score, radiotherapy dose fractionation employed (3 week versus 1 week), age, breast surgery type (Breast conservation vs Mastectomy), nodal staging type (axillary dissection versus sentinel lymph node biopsy) and regional nodal radiotherapy (delivered or not). Age will be modelled flexibly using restricted cubic splines with 4 knots. Graphical depiction of the patient-reported outcome scores over the assessment period will be provided. Missing data at each assessment time will be reported at the level of the instrument as well as at the level of the individual items. Based on the kind of dropout experienced for the patient-reported outcome an alternative joint model where the death or disease recurrence can stop the observation of the longitudinal outcome would also be considered. This will be used if the dropout in the QoL assessments is related to the disease recurrence or death in the trial. Graphical and tabular overview of the mean scores for each scale at the measurement timepoints will also be provided.

sec.title: Clinician-reported toxicity
sec.p: Clinician-reported toxicity will be recorded using the same CRF as used in the current HYPORT Adjuvant trial. This will serve as a secondary reporting of the toxicity measures along with the patient-reported outcomes. Comparison and reporting will follow the same principles as patient reported outcome noted above.

sec.title: Perforator detection rate
sec.p: This would be reported as a crude proportion of patients where perforators were detected. No specific model would be required for this endpoint.

sec.title: Sentinel detection rate
sec.p: Crude proportions of patients where sentinel lymph nodes were not detected would be reported for the arms (NART vs ART). Comparison between arms will be done using a proportional odds model with an adjustment for the dose fractionation schema employed. Odds and 95% confidence intervals of the estimates will be reported.

sec.title: Wound complication rate
sec.p: Crude proportion of patients experiencing wound complication will be reported for each arm. Wound complication rate will be compared between the radiotherapy sequence (NART vs ART) using a proportional odds model with an adjustment for the dose fractionation schema employed. The independent variable of interest will be the proportion of patients with surgical wound complications graded using the 5-point Calvien Dindo rating scale [38]. The maximum grade of these complications experienced over a 12-week period post-surgery will be analysed. Odds ratio and 95% confidence intervals of the estimates will be reported.

sec.title: Pathological complete response
sec.p: Pathological complete response is an outcome of interest for the second substudy and will be defined as absence of invasive cancer in breast and the lymph nodes [36]. Pathological complete response rates will be presented for each arm separately and compared between the radiotherapy sequence (NART vs ART) using a logistic regression model adjusted for the dose fractionation employed, grade, breast cancer subtype, clinical T stage and clinical N stage. Odds ratio and 95% confidence intervals of the estimate will be reported. Additional reporting of the pathological complete response in the breast will also be done and compared between the two arms using the same method.

The residual cancer burden (RCB) will also be reported for all three arms and compared between the two radiotherapy sequences (NART vs ART) using a proportional odds model with an adjustment for the dose fractionation employed, grade, breast cancer subtype, clinical T stage and clinical N stage.

sec.title: Interim analyses {21b}
sec.p: Two interim analyses have been planned as noted in the section on sample size calculation for the primary endpoint of 3-year DFS. These will be conducted when the required number of events have accumulated and are projected to occur at 42 and 55 months. Additionally reporting of the outcomes from the wound complication substudy and pathological complete response rate substudies will be done as per schedule.

sec.title: Methods for additional analyses (e.g. subgroup analyses) {20b}
sec.p: Additional subgroup analysis in the form of evaluation of the heterogeneity of treatment effect between arms for the cancer outcomes will be undertaken for the following subgroups:

list-item.p: Menopausal Status: Premenopausal vs Postmenopausal
Axillary staging: Axillary dissection versus sentinel node biopsy
Subtype: Luminal vs Her2-enriched vs TNBC
Regional Nodal Radiation: None vs supraclavicular fossa (SCF) alone vs SCF + Internal mammary (IMN) vs SCF + IMN + Axillary irradiation
Boost Type: SIB vs Sequential Boost

sec.title: Methods in analysis to handle protocol non-adherence and any statistical methods to handle missing data {20c}
sec.p: Every effort should be made to ensure that patient data is complete. However, in a vast country like India with an inadequate primary health care system missing data due to loss to follow-up is expected. For each of the time to event endpoints, if the number of patients with missing data is more than 10% then an additional sensitivity analysis will be undertaken where all such patients with missing data would be considered to have the event of interest. For patient-reported endpoints, analysis of the missing data will be based on the principles outlined by the SISAQOL consortium.

sec.title: Plans to give access to the full protocol, participant-level data and statistical code {31c}
sec.p: Access to the full protocol will be available through our published manuscript. Individual patient-level data and statistical code can be shared on request.

sec.title: Composition of the coordinating centre and trial steering committee {5d}
sec.p: Tata medical centre will be the coordinating centre. The trial steering committee will comprise investigators from each participating centre.

sec.title: Composition of the data monitoring committee, its role and reporting structure {21a}
sec.p: A formal data monitoring committee will be established for the study. The Data Monitoring and Safety Committee (DMSC) constituted for the trial will be responsible for monitoring the trial and the overall responsibility of monitoring the trial will be borne by the CTU. The DSMC will also review the conduct of the trial and recommend continuation or stopping based on the results of the pre-planned analyses. Monitoring will include centralised review of CRFs and other study documents for protocol compliance, data accuracy and completeness. Monitoring may include monitoring visits to investigational sites for source data verification, review of the investigator’s site file and radiotherapy records. The monitoring staff will be given direct access to source documents, CRFs and other study-related documents. By signing the informed consent form, the subject gives authorised monitoring staff direct access to their medical records and the study data.

Compliance to protocol will be reviewed after accrual of the first 50 cases. Any protocol deviation needs to be notified to the respective IRB, to the chief investigator, coordinating centre and discussed in the TMG meetings. Additionally, PI at each centre should be notified about any changes made to the protocol in the interest of patient safety as this will need updating in writing in the trial protocol with a change in the version number of the study protocol. Any major radiation dosimetric protocol deviation in more than 1 patient of the first 5 patients or more than 10% cases after 10 have been recruited, should be reported to and discussed by the Trial management committee.

sec.title: Adverse event
sec.p: An ADVERSE EVENT (AE) is any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical investigational subject administered a pharmaceutical product and which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with this treatment. An AE can therefore be any unfavourable or unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding), symptom or disease temporally associated with the use of a medicinal investigational product, whether or not considered related to the medicinal product (see below).
Adverse events include the following:

list-item.p: All suspected adverse drug or device reactions
All reactions from drug or device
Overdose, abuse, withdrawal, sensitivity, toxicity or failure of expected pharmacological action (if appropriate)
Apparently unrelated illnesses, including the worsening (severity, frequency) of pre-existing illnesses
Injury or accidents.
Abnormalities in physiological testing or physical examination that require clinical intervention or further investigation (beyond ordering a repeat examination)
Laboratory abnormalities that require clinical intervention or further investigation (beyond ordering a laboratory test).
Any untoward event that occurs after the protocol-specified reporting period which the Investigator believes may be related to the drug or device.

sec.p: AEs must be reported as AEs even if they do not meet SAE criteria.

sec.title: Serious adverse events
sec.p: An SAE is any untoward medical occurrence which results in:

list-item.p: Death
Is life-threatening (i.e. the subject was at risk of death at the time of the event)
Requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation
Results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity
Other important medical events which, in the opinion of the investigator, are likely to become serious if untreated, or as defined in the protocol

sec.p: Important medical events which may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation but may jeopardise the patient or may require intervention to prevent one of the listed outcomes in the definition above should also be considered serious.

sec.title: Suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction (SUSAR)
sec.p: A SUSAR is an SAE that is related to the drug or device and is unexpected (i.e. not listed in the investigator brochure or approved Product Information; or is not listed at the specificity or severity that has been observed; or is not consistent with the risk information described in the Subject Information Sheet and Informed Consent Form or elsewhere in the protocol. (FDA, Safety Reporting Requirements for INDs and BA/BE Studies, draft guidance, September 2010)).

An event is causally related if there is a reasonable possibility that the drug [intervention] caused the AE, i.e. there is evidence to suggest a causal relationship between the drug and the event (FDA, Safety Reporting Requirements for INDs and BA/BE Studies, draft guidance, September 2010).
The following events will not be reported as SAEs:

list-item.p: Hospitalisation to deliver study procedures
Hospitalisation to treat disease progression
Unrelated scheduled elective surgery
Convenience purposes, e.g. transportation issues/blood transfusions.

sec.title: Reporting of SAE
sec.p: The investigator at each site is responsible for reporting the SAE to the respective Institutional Review Board as well as the PI at the CTU. Local IRB should be notified of any SAE within 24 h on a working day or as per the institutional norm. The CTU should be intimated within a period of 10 days from the date of occurrence of the SAE. SAEs must be reported up to 30 days from the end of study intervention.
The following information should be provided for all SAEs:

list-item.p: Event description including classification according to NCI CTCAE
Primary and secondary diagnosis of the event (If death/hospitalisation)
Severity/Worst Grade
Attribution to study intervention
Expectedness (listed in IB/product information)
Action taken with study intervention
Impact of SAE (e.g. hospitalisation details)
The outcome of SAE including end date if recovered

sec.title: Frequency and plans for auditing trial conduct {23}
sec.p: The study may be subject to audit and inspection by the representatives of the regulatory bodies which may include hospital level Institutional review board, stage regulatory bodies and national regulatory bodies.

sec.title: Plans for communicating important protocol amendments to relevant parties (e.g. trial participants, ethical committees) {25}
sec.p: This study will be conducted according to the Note for Guidance on Good Clinical Practice provided by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) and in compliance with applicable laws and regulations. The study will be performed in accordance with the principles laid down by the World Medical Assembly in the Declaration of Helsinki 2004. The investigators shall comply with the protocol, except when a protocol deviation is required to eliminate immediate hazard to a subject. In this circumstance, the local IRB and the trial CTU should be notified immediately.

sec.title: Protocol amendments
sec.p: Any modifications to the protocol which impacts the conduct of study, or affects patient safety, including changes in the objectives, design, eligibility criteria, sample size, study procedures or major changes will require a formal amendment to the protocol. Any such amendment must be agreed upon by the trial management committee and approved by the Institutional Review Board of the participating centre(s) prior to implementation.

sec.title: Dissemination policy {31a}
sec.p: The Trial Management Committee will appoint a Writing Committee to draft manuscript(s) based on the trial data. Manuscript(s) will be submitted to peer-reviewed journal(s). The Writing Committee will develop a publication plan, including authorship, target journals and expected dates of publication. All publications must receive prior written approval from the TMC prior to submission.

sec.title: Clinical study report
sec.p: A Clinical Study Report which summarises and interprets all the pertinent study data collected will be issued which may form the basis of manuscript(s) intended for publication. The Clinical Study Report or summary thereof will be provided to the local IRB of the institutes participating in the protocol. Additionally the same will be made available on the trial registration websites.

sec.title: Data Availability Statement
sec.p: Intra-study data sharing will be done with input from the Trial management committee. All site PIs will be provided with access to the cleaned dataset. All project data will be housed in the institutional REDCap installation available at Tata Medical Center. Data access groups will be used to restrict access to the institutional data to individual institutions. Minimum identifying personal information will be stored.
